card.name: Gandagana
card.profile: Gandagana is a popular Georgian folk song and traditional dance from Adjara, the basis of the staged Acharuli Gandagana (Wikipedia; Georgia Today). The staged dance was introduced to wide audiences in 1946 by choreographer Enver Khabadze after an expedition to the village of Khulo; Guliko Nogaideli and Topan Meladze were among the first duet dancers. It is characterized by elegant, lighthearted flirtation between a young man and woman, with lateral and progressive steps; the name relates to the Georgian 'ghani' (width). The polyphonic song's refrain 'Tarnanani ninano' evokes an eternal farewell between separated lovers.
card.insight: The Adjarian Gandagana has the status of a Monument of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Georgia, and gained global exposure when French-Congolese rapper GIMS released 'Ninao' on 20 February 2025, taking much of its melody from the traditional Gandagana folk song (Georgia Today; Wikipedia, 'Ninao').
card.image_significance: Adjara's playful love song-dance. A representative image shows upright carriage, sweeping arm lines and embroidered dress — Adjara, Georgia.
